name: Prey
overview: Prey climbs a 5-pitch (510 ft), mostly-bolted line up corners, roofs, and an arete on the right side of Osprey Wall on quality white marbled rock, highlighted by a celebrated 5.10c third pitch, the "money pitch."
beta: A series of corners, overhangs, and slabs to the top of Osprey Wall with excellent crystal pocket holds; protection is a mix of bolts and natural gear, with the third pitch fully bolted. Pitch 1 ("First Flight," 5.6) is a bolted slab ending in a chute; P2 (5.9+) climbs a right-facing corner with a roof and bolted slab; P3 (5.10c, "the money pitch") features roof systems and an arete on white marbled rock; P4 (5.9) follows a corner ramp becoming an open book (with two variations); P5 (5.10c) finishes on an arete.
descent_text: From the top of the wall, double-rope rappels (two 60 m ropes) from tree anchors on climber's left lead back down, trending slightly left to the next ledge — inspect any fixed gear before trusting it due to reported pika damage at anchors. Alternatively, descend the scree slope, using the full rope length as a handline/backup if downclimbing.
descent: Rappel/scree descent from the top of the wall.
rappels: Double-rope (60m) rappels from fixed tree anchors, trending left tree-to-tree back to lower ledges.
rappel_count_note: The number of rappels is not published. The descent starts from a tree anchor on climber's left of the final belay and continues tree to tree on two 60 m ropes, trending slightly left to each lower ledge. Inspect the fixed slings before use; damage from pikas has been reported at the anchors.

pitch_detail.notes: Scramble up dirty ledges until the first bolt shows on the cleanest black-and-white granite, then follow bolts up the slab into a chute between two stands of trees. Exit right, then shift the belay uphill and left to sit beneath a right-facing corner.
Stem the brown right-facing corner up to a roof; the crux moves here are exposed but well protected. Above the roof step right onto a short bolted slab. Bolts plus a few optional small cams or nuts.

The only fully bolted pitch: steep, thoughtful corner climbing on white marbled rock through two roof sections, finishing on a sustained arête face. A #1 or #2 cam is optional near the top. Stated length for this pitch varies between roughly 30 and 40 m.

Follow the corner ramp as it trends right and steepens into an open book, mixing bolts and gear. A variation traverses out to a slung horn for more exposure; either way ends at the belay below the final arête.
Three bolts up a short, fun arête to the top anchor. Leave a #1 cam in the overhang section to protect the follower. The double-rope rappel starts from a tree anchor above this belay.

fa: Christian Junkar, Tom Beirne, and Mik Metzler, Aug 2020
